headline: Ship the interaction tier in two honest phases. Phase 1 (v1, first-class) is ONLY what the user explicitly asked for: a tiny zero-dependency Skyline.Interaction holding the approval decision model behind one IApprovalUi seam, a default InProcessShell (no Akka), and a desktop ApprovalsOverlay that composites through the EXISTING BeginClearPass=false path — no new FrameLoop hook, no Akka, no FocusGraph/Target/Command/Transfer/Intent vocabulary, no async-state-machine surface beyond a single TaskCompletionSource the tests drive directly. Phase 2 promotes the full primitive guide, the Akka runtime, and the zero-copy GPU transfer bridge only when Starling actually demands the primitive surface. This resolves every blocker: the Akka-is-mandatory inversion, the iOS one-thread deadlock, the snapshot multi-writer race, the await-then-mutate actor bug, the OnOverlay opaque-present reachability violation, the GPU-texture-round-trip contradiction, and the cover.sh coverage gate — by deferring the heavy machinery rather than shipping it half-correct.
finalLayering:
Six tiers, top to bottom, with the interaction tier strictly OPTIONAL and ADDITIVE.

CORE THREE (unchanged, no interaction vocabulary, no Akka, ever):
- Skyline (window host): keeps emitting plain PointerEvent/KeyEvent/TextEvent and a plain ClipboardText string. Gains nothing. The only planned additions stay plain input facts (key modifier state, pointer enter/leave).
- Skyline.Gpu (1:1 wgpu mirror): raw Silk.NET handles in/out. No Actor/Focus/Target/Command/Transfer/Capability/Consent type may appear.
- Skyline.Render (frame owner): FrameLoop owns pace->acquire->clear pass->OnRender->end->submit->present. In v1 it gains ZERO new members. The overlay composites through the already-shipped BeginClearPass=false path (FrameLoopOptions.cs:24, Frame.Encoder/View public on Frame.cs:30-43). The OnOverlay hook is REJECTED for v1 (see keptRejected) because the THREADING + DESIGN-RULE reviewers proved it either presents overlay pixels behind the consumer's back (no present seam between DriveFrame line 211's present() and the overlay encode) or duplicates a solved path, and the SCOPE reviewer proved it is unnecessary core API creep with no caller the existing path can't serve.

INTERACTION TIER (optional, added above Skyline.Render):
- Skyline.Interaction (ZERO family deps — no Skyline, Gpu, Render, Silk.NET, Akka): the pure decision vocabulary and the default in-process shell. In v1 this is small: Actor/ActorKind/ActorLocality, InteractionCapability flags, CapabilityGrant, ConsentRecord, ApprovalRequest/ApprovalDecision/ApprovalVerb, the ApprovalState union (Pending/Granted/Denied/Expired modeled on FrameOutcome's union(Ok,Err)), IApprovalPolicy + DefaultApprovalPolicy, IApprovalUi, and a minimal InProcessApprovalShell. TimeProvider is injected so every deadline/expiry branch is fake-clock testable. The full guide (FocusGraph six slots, Target hierarchy, CommandId, Transfer broker, Intents, InputSnapshot, the three async shell interfaces) is DEFERRED to Phase 2 and lives here when built.
- Skyline.Interaction.Ui (the ONLY pixel-bearing assembly; deps: Skyline.Interaction + Skyline.Render + Skyline.Gpu + Skyline): the composited ApprovalsOverlay implementing IApprovalUi, plus AppWindowInteractionSource (the desktop input/clipboard glue). The hit-test + state machine are extracted into a pure, GPU-free, headless-testable class; only the wgpu encode is windowed.
- Skyline.Interaction.Akka (DEFERRED to Phase 2; deps: Skyline.Interaction + Akka.NET only, never Render/Gpu/Skyline): the supervised actor runtime, opt-in for remote/collaboration/multi-actor scale. NOT a v1 dependency of anything.

iOS path drops the window host and render tiers entirely: Skyline.Gpu (via GpuContext.Create(wgpu, surfaceFactory) off CAMetalLayer, verified in PageRenderer.cs:160) + Skyline.Interaction + a native UIKitApprovalUi that lives in the iOS APP/SAMPLE project, never in a shipped Skyline assembly.

ARCHITECTURE.md line 146 ("a library that owns the frame... never inside them") is REWRITTEN, not designed around: a Skyline-family layer MAY own, composite, and present the frame (FrameLoop already does); the live rule is REACHABILITY — raw wgpu, raw input, and a runtime-free primitives package each stay one property or one reference away; only HIDING wgpu is forbidden.

FrameLoop frame ownership + BeginClearPass=false compositing path + Frame raw Pass/View/Encoder. v1: ZERO new members.

Pure decision vocabulary + default in-process approval shell. v1 set: Actor, ActorKind, ActorLocality, InteractionCapability[Flags], CapabilityGrant, ConsentRecord, ApprovalRequest, ApprovalDecision, ApprovalVerb, ApprovalState union, IApprovalPolicy, DefaultApprovalPolicy, IApprovalUi, InProcessApprovalShell, injected TimeProvider. Phase 2 adds FocusGraph/Target/CommandId/Transfer/Intents/InputSnapshot + the three async shell interfaces HERE when a real caller needs them.
projectLayout.dependsOn: NOTHING in the family. net11.0 only. No Silk.NET, no Akka. C# 15 unions for closed sets.

projectLayout.owns: Composited ApprovalsOverlay : IApprovalUi (the desktop battery), the GPU-free ApprovalSurfaceState hit-test/stack/expire core (headless-testable), and AppWindowInteractionSource (subscribes to AppWindow.PointerInput/KeyInput/TextInput; wraps ClipboardText behind an injectable IClipboard so the sync/fallback logic is headless-covered against a fake). Composites via BeginClearPass=false / Frame.Encoder — opens a LoadOp.Load pass, no new FrameLoop member.

Supervised actor runtime: ShellActor/FocusActor/BrokerActor/SurfaceActor/InputSourceActor tree, single-writer FocusActor, identity-from-Sender enforcement, park-the-asker approval suspend (no await-then-mutate). Opt-in scale-up for remote/collaboration only.

Folded into Skyline.Interaction.Ui. The fourth-project split is rejected for v1: AppWindowInteractionSource is a thin adapter and the input-without-overlay use case has no v1 caller. Revisit only if a consumer needs the desktop input bridge without the renderer.

UIKitApprovalUi : IApprovalUi (UIAlertController), UIKit input source, UIPasteboard clipboard. PLATFORM presentation lives in the app/sample, never in a shipped Skyline assembly, so the one-exclusion (Guard.cs) coverage invariant holds.

primitiveMap.binding: Pure record + enums in Skyline.Interaction (v1). On desktop the local human Actor{Human,Local} is minted by AppWindowInteractionSource. Identity is a data field in v1 (InProcessShell trusts the caller). When Akka lands (Phase 2), locality MUST be derived from Sender.Path, never the spoofable ActorId field — this fixes the THREADING reviewer's major identity-spoof hole. AI/remote are real separate actors with addresses then, never faked as a local mouse.

Pure types in Skyline.Interaction (v1). The three named scenarios collapse to ONE parameterized prompt: 'request control' = Administer (and/or Point|Navigation|Capture), 'access the keyboard' = LowLevelInput, 'wants to type' = Edit. RequiresVisibleUi routes to the overlay. Enforced in InProcessShell (v1) / at the actor boundary (Phase 2).

Pure (Actor, InteractionCapability) -> PolicyOutcome union(ImplicitGrant, Ask, Deny) in Skyline.Interaction. Keyed on (ActorKind, ActorLocality). Local human implicit-grants ordinary capability; Ai/Automation get Ask; nobody gets LowLevelInput/Edit/Administer without a prompt; remote human is capped to Point/Select/Collaborate and hard-Denied Edit/LowLevelInput. Fully overridable (shell.Policy = myPolicy). Headless-testable to 100%.
C# 15 union in Skyline.Interaction, mirroring FrameOutcome's union(Ok, Err). The render thread and resolver branch exhaustively. Pure, headless-testable.

In Skyline.Interaction. RequestAsync(ApprovalRequest, ct) -> Task<ApprovalDecision>. ApprovalsOverlay (composited desktop battery) and UIKitApprovalUi (native iOS, in the app project) are interchangeable implementations. A consumer who wants its own chrome implements IApprovalUi and never references Skyline.Interaction.Ui.

In Skyline.Interaction.Ui. Reads ONE immutable ApprovalSurfaceState off a single volatile field (mirroring AppWindow's FrameGeom, AppWindow.cs:26), early-outs allocation-free when nothing is pending, and composites via the existing BeginClearPass=false path: the consumer calls overlay.Encode(frame) from their own OnRender (or for a clear-pass app, the overlay is given the encoder/view through Frame). It opens a LoadOp.Load pass against Frame.View — never wraps or hides it.

AppWindowInteractionSource subscribes to AppWindow.PointerInput/KeyInput (fire on MAIN thread per the contract); pointer-down hit-tests the cached button rects and resolves the TaskCompletionSource. Raw events stay public and unintercepted — the source SUBSCRIBES.

v1: stays a plain string property. The text-transfer story is deferred to Phase 2's broker. When the broker lands, it wraps ClipboardText behind an injectable IClipboard (so sync/fallback is headless-covered against a fake) and routes the GLFW-bound set/get through AppHost.Invoke with a timeout so a stalled pump denies rather than hangs — fixing the THREADING reviewer's liveness-coupling finding.

primitiveMap.primitive: FocusGraph / Target / CommandId / Transfer broker / Intents / InputSnapshot / async shell interfaces
primitiveMap.binding: DEFERRED to Phase 2 (see phasing). Built in Skyline.Interaction when Starling demands the primitive surface. Documented north star, not v1 code, so the 100% coverage gate stays cheap and no speculative type is built for an input (gaze tracker, speech engine, remote transport) that has zero implementation in the repo today.

DEFERRED + scoped. The v1 transfer story is text/metadata only and says so plainly. ITransferRepresentation.OpenReadAsync returns a byte Stream, which would force a GPU->CPU round-trip (forbidden by project memory). The GPU-handle representation lives in a future Skyline.Interaction.Gpu bridge (depends on Skyline.Gpu, keeps Skyline.Interaction GPU-free). Until that bridge exists, surface copy/paste is explicitly NOT claimed first-class.

approvalsFlow:
ONE prompt, one record, one state machine for all three scenarios, driven by CapabilityGrant flags (request-control=Administer, keyboard=LowLevelInput, type=Edit), each RequiresVisibleUi=true.

THREADING HANDOFF (desktop, two threads — main + render):
1. REQUEST originates on the shell's thread. InProcessApprovalShell.AuthorizeAsync evaluates the policy. ImplicitGrant short-circuits to Granted with ConsentRecord{PolicyAllowed} and draws nothing. Deny rejects without ever reaching the UI. Ask calls IApprovalUi.RequestAsync.
2. IApprovalUi.RequestAsync (ApprovalsOverlay) creates a TaskCompletionSource<ApprovalDecision>(RunContinuationsAsynchronously), registers it keyed by request id, and — CRITICAL FIX for the THREADING reviewer's snapshot multi-writer race — does NOT rebuild the snapshot itself from an arbitrary thread. Instead it posts the request to a SINGLE OWNER (in v1, a lock-guarded mutation method in the shell; in Phase 2, the gate actor), which rebuilds the immutable ApprovalSurfaceState and swaps it into the volatile field. One writer, exactly like AppWindow's FrameGeom. Then RequestRedraw() (any-thread-safe, AppWindow.cs:156).
3. The OVERLAY draws on the RENDER thread inside the consumer's OnRender (BeginClearPass=false path). It reads one volatile snapshot (atomic load, tear-free because the snapshot is immutable), early-returns allocation-free when nothing pending, else opens a LoadOp.Load pass on Frame.Encoder against Frame.View. It NEVER touches the TaskCompletionSource and NEVER resolves anything — the render thread only reads (this fixes the reviewer's 'render thread must not resolve TCS' finding).
4. The ANSWER arrives on the MAIN thread: AppWindow.PointerInput fires during PollEvents, AppWindowInteractionSource hit-tests cached button rects, and calls Resolve. Resolve does tcs.TrySetResult(decision) (thread-safe) which unblocks the awaiting shell on a thread-pool thread, then posts the snapshot rebuild to the single owner and requests one more redraw to clear the modal.
5. DEADLINE/CANCEL: every ApprovalRequest carries ExpiresAt driven by the injected TimeProvider. A scheduled timeout (Phase 2: Akka scheduler; v1: a TimeProvider-backed timer) resolves any unanswered request to Deny so no caller hangs. Pruning clears the persistent indicator. The CancellationToken path also resolves to Deny. Both paths are headless-testable with a fake clock — no wall-clock race.

CONCURRENT/STACKED REQUESTS: surfaced FIFO (not LIFO top-of-stack), every parked request has its own independent TaskCompletionSource and its own timeout, prune-on-resolve immediately surfaces the next. This fixes the DESIGN-RULE reviewer's starvation/liveness finding.

NON-REPLACING OBSERVE/VETO SEAM: a consumer keeping the default battery gets a BeforeGrant callback (returns bool to veto) and a GrantMinted event, so an individual decision is observable/vetoable without forking IApprovalPolicy or IApprovalUi — fixing the DESIGN-RULE reviewer's wholesale-only-eject minor finding.

iOS PATH (ONE thread — the run loop, verified: BrowserViewController.OnFrame, OnPan, and ShouldReturn all run on NSRunLoop.Main): there is NO render thread and NO FrameLoop. The shell MUST NOT be awaited synchronously on the main run loop or it deadlocks (the run loop is blocked, OnFrame never runs, the UIAlertController action never fires, the TCS never resolves — exactly the THREADING reviewer's blocker). So: (a) IApprovalUi is UIKitApprovalUi (in the app/sample project, not a shipped assembly), whose RequestAsync marshals to the UIKit main run loop via DispatchQueue.MainQueue, presents a UIAlertController, and resolves the TCS from the tap action — all genuinely async, yielding back to the run loop; (b) the shell's awaits are real async and never blocked on main; (c) the composited overlay is simply not used — native chrome over the wgpu page is the platform convention (the existing address-bar pattern). The decision logic (policy, capability, consent) is byte-for-byte identical and pixel-free; only the presentation differs.
akkaTopology:
DEFERRED to Phase 2. Akka is the opt-in scale-up for remote/collaboration/multi-actor, NOT a v1 dependency of anything (this resolves the unanimous reviewer finding that making Akka the only shell inverts batteries-with-eject: the battery becomes too big to be the default). The v1 default shell is the plain InProcessApprovalShell in Skyline.Interaction, zero extra deps.

When Phase 2 lands, the SETTLED topology (folding in the THREADING reviewer's fixes):

TREE (one window, desktop):
/user/shell                  ShellActor      (PinnedDispatcher 'shell-dispatcher': arbitration, grant table, approval suspend)
  /user/shell/focus          FocusActor      (single writer of FocusGraph)
  /user/shell/broker         BrokerActor     (transfer offers + policy; clipboard mirror via AppHost.Invoke WITH timeout)
  /user/shell/approvals      ApprovalGate    (SOLE writer of the approval snapshot; owns timeouts via the Akka scheduler)
  /user/shell/sources/*      InputSourceActor per modality (mouse/voice/gaze/ai:*/remote:*) — each guide Actor = one address
  /user/shell/surfaces/*     SurfaceActor per IInteractiveSurface (bridges to render thread by snapshot + RequestRedraw, never wgpu)

PROTOCOL: immutable records. Tell for fire-and-forget input (UpdatePointer/UpdateAttention/SetCapture), Ask->PipeTo for commands. ApprovalRequested/ApprovalAnswered are MESSAGES.

THREADING BRIDGE (the load-bearing part, with reviewer fixes baked in):
1. Input (MAIN) -> mailbox: AppWindow events fire on main; the source actor.Tell()s; the main thread never blocks on a dispatcher.
2. Dispatcher -> MAIN (windowing/GLFW/clipboard): marshal via IMainThread.Post = AppHost.Invoke, and every value-returning GLFW op (clipboard GET) is wrapped Invoke(() => tcs.TrySetResult(window.ClipboardText)) WITH a timeout so a stalled pump denies rather than hangs.
3. Dispatcher -> RENDER (drawing): NEVER call wgpu from a Receive. Flip an immutable snapshot (volatile swap, one writer) + call RequestRedraw. The render thread reads the snapshot in OnRender.
4. NEVER block a dispatcher on a render result, and NEVER Ask().Result on the PinnedDispatcher (self-deadlock). 
5. APPROVAL SUSPEND uses PARK-THE-ASKER, NOT await-then-mutate. The ShellActor stashes (Sender, request) keyed by ApprovalId and returns immediately; ApprovalAnswered un-stashes ON the dispatcher and mutates _grants/_pending THERE. The approvals-facet's `await _ui.RequestAsync(...).ConfigureAwait(false); MakeGrant()` pattern is DELETED — ConfigureAwait(false) + RunContinuationsAsynchronously moves the continuation off the pinned thread and races actor state (the THREADING reviewer's blocker). Awaiting external work inside an actor and then touching actor state is forbidden.
6. IDENTITY: locality/kind derived from Sender.Path (Akka-authenticated), never the spoofable ActorId message field. The FocusActor validates Context.Sender is the expected local source before writing the local Pointer/Text slots — that is what makes 'a remote pointer cannot steal local focus' structural, not a convention.
7. SNAPSHOT has exactly ONE writer (the ApprovalGate actor), restoring the FrameGeom single-writer invariant the desktop facet broke with two writers.
8. RESTART SAFETY: on PreRestart/PostStop the gate drains _pending and completes every parked Task with denied, so a supervised AI restart strands no caller.

iOS: same ShellActor/FocusActor/BrokerActor run unchanged on Akka dispatchers (never inline on the main run loop). IMainThread.Post becomes DispatchQueue.MainQueue. CADisplayLink drives the frame; no FrameLoop. This portability is exactly why the runtime carries zero Skyline/Render dependency.

COVERAGE: 100% of decision logic stays as pure functions / the InProcessShell in Skyline.Interaction, driven headless. Akka actor bodies are one-line handlers calling already-covered pure functions; the thin actor glue (supervision restart, stash/un-stash, timeout, spoof-reject) is covered with Akka.TestKit using TestScheduler.Advance (no wall-clock race) in a separate headless test project.

phasing.phase: v1 / Phase 1 — first-class, ship now (minimum viable integration the user explicitly asked for)
phasing.deliverable: Skyline.Interaction (zero deps): Actor + capability/grant/consent + ApprovalRequest/Decision + ApprovalState union + IApprovalPolicy/DefaultApprovalPolicy + IApprovalUi + InProcessApprovalShell + injected TimeProvider. Skyline.Interaction.Ui: composited ApprovalsOverlay : IApprovalUi via the EXISTING BeginClearPass=false path (no new FrameLoop member), a GPU-free ApprovalSurfaceState (hit-test/stack/expire, headless-tested), AppWindowInteractionSource with injectable IClipboard. iOS UIKitApprovalUi in the app/sample. ARCHITECTURE.md line 146 rewrite. cover.sh amended to add the two new assemblies to both --include and -assemblyfilters; two FrameLoop tests are NOT needed because no FrameLoop member changes.
phasing.rationale: Satisfies 'Skyline owns the approvals UI' for the three named scenarios on desktop and iOS, with the smallest surface that honors batteries-with-eject. No Akka (avoids the heavy-default inversion), no new core-three API (avoids the OnOverlay reachability + scope violations), no async beyond one TCS the tests drive directly (the repo has zero async precedent — keep it tiny and fake-clock-deterministic), no speculative vocabulary (keeps the 100% gate cheap). The new tier is small and additive, not an order of magnitude larger than the library it sits on.

phasing.phase: v2 / Phase 2 — promote when Starling demands the primitive surface
phasing.deliverable: In Skyline.Interaction: FocusGraph (six slots + BestCommandTarget pure fn), Target hierarchy + TargetRef, CommandId/CommandDescriptor/CommandRequest/CommandResult, TransferOffer/Policy/Provenance/Scope + ITransferBroker, Intents + InputSnapshot, the three async shell interfaces (IInteractionShell/IInteractiveSurface/ITransferBroker). Each primitive added when its first real caller arrives.
phasing.rationale: The full guide is a documented north star, not a v1 burden. Nothing in the only concrete consumer (Starling, Picture B, iOS) asks for six focus slots, Ray3D/Volume3D targets, 11 intent verbs, or seven transfer scopes yet — and there is no gaze tracker, speech engine, AI actor, or remote transport in the repo to exercise them. Building vocabulary for inputs that do not exist is over-engineering against a gated 100% coverage requirement.

phasing.deliverable: Skyline.Interaction.Akka: ShellActor/FocusActor/BrokerActor/SurfaceActor/source actors, single-writer FocusActor, Sender-path identity, park-the-asker suspend, single-writer approval-snapshot gate, restart-drains-parked-callers, scheduler-driven timeouts. Akka.TestKit coverage with TestScheduler.Advance.
phasing.rationale: Akka earns its keep only at remote/collaboration/multi-mailbox scale, which v1 does not need. It is the scale-up transport, swapped in by reference change because the policy/arbitration rules live as pure functions in Skyline.Interaction that both shells share.

phasing.phase: v2+ / Phase 2 later — zero-copy GPU transfer bridge
phasing.deliverable: Skyline.Interaction.Gpu: a GPU-handle representation interface (yields a wgpu Texture*/TextureView*) so AgentStaging/DragDropSession surface transfers never round-trip to CPU. Depends on Skyline.Gpu; keeps Skyline.Interaction GPU-free.
phasing.rationale: ITransferRepresentation.OpenReadAsync's byte Stream cannot carry the one payload Starling moves zero-copy (project memory: textures must never round-trip to CPU). Until this bridge exists, the transfer broker is honestly scoped to text/metadata — do not claim surface copy/paste is first-class.

kept: The hard split keeping the core three uncorrupted: Skyline.Gpu stays a 1:1 wgpu mirror, Skyline keeps plain input structs + ClipboardText, interaction vocabulary lives one tier up. All four reviewers affirm this and it is verified against source.

Zero-dependency Skyline.Interaction as the pure decision tier — usable headless, on iOS, in MSTest. The single best coverage decision; enforce it ruthlessly (any branch that can be a pure function must be).
IApprovalUi as the eject seam with two interchangeable batteries (composited desktop overlay, native UIKitApprovalUi). Unanimously cited as the best idea and the v1 centerpiece.
The three scenarios collapsing into ONE parameterized prompt driven by CapabilityGrant flags (Administer/LowLevelInput/Edit). Elegant and minimal.
The (ActorKind, ActorLocality) default policy table with overridable DefaultApprovalPolicy and the structural rule that remote/AI never get Edit/LowLevelInput. Does not need actors to be true.
The immutable-snapshot-swapped-through-one-volatile-field pattern (ApprovalSurfaceState mirroring AppWindow's FrameGeom), with allocation-free idle path, AS LONG AS there is exactly ONE writer.
ApprovalsOverlay.Encode taking raw TextureView*/CommandEncoder* (not a WindowSurface) so the GPU draw path is headless-coverable via CreateForTest + TextureReadback like FrameLoopTests.
Subscribe-not-replace for raw input and the raw-frame-stays-reachable compositing posture (overlay reads the same View via a LoadOp.Load pass, never wraps it).
ARCHITECTURE.md line 146 rewrite: a Skyline-family layer MAY own/composite/present the frame; the live rule is reachability; only hiding wgpu is forbidden.
Mapping each guide Actor 1:1 to an addressable Akka actor and the single-writer FocusActor — KEPT but DEFERRED to Phase 2, and with the fix that identity comes from Sender.Path not the message field.
rejected: FrameLoop.OnOverlay hook in v1. REJECTED. Three reviewers converge: it either presents overlay pixels with no consumer-visible/overridable present (DriveFrame line 211's present() has no seam after the overlay encode — a 'nothing presented behind your back' violation), or it duplicates the already-solved BeginClearPass=false path, and it is net-new permanent public API in the most load-bearing core file with no caller the existing path can't serve, plus it adds required-covered lines to a core-three assembly the design pledges to barely touch. Route the overlay through BeginClearPass=false. Revisit only if a real clear-pass app proves ergonomic pain.

Akka as the only / default IInteractionShell. REJECTED for v1. Making a heavy actor framework mandatory to get any working shell inverts batteries-with-eject. The InProcessApprovalShell (lock-guarded, no Akka) is the v1 default; Akka is the opt-in Phase 2 scale-up.

The approvals-facet ApprovalGate.AuthorizeAsync that does `await _ui.RequestAsync(...).ConfigureAwait(false)` then mutates shell state. REJECTED as a correctness bug — the continuation runs off the pinned dispatcher and races actor state. Replaced by the Akka-facet park-the-asker pattern as the single canonical design.

Two writers of the approval snapshot (RequestAsync on an arbitrary thread AND Resolve on main). REJECTED — breaks the FrameGeom single-writer invariant and can lose updates. All snapshot mutation goes through one owner.
LIFO top-of-stack (Pending[^1]) surfacing of concurrent requests. REJECTED for starvation/liveness — replaced by FIFO with per-request independent timeouts and prune-on-resolve.

Building the full primitive guide (FocusGraph/Target/CommandId/Transfer/Intents/InputSnapshot + three async shell interfaces) in v1. REJECTED as speculative generality against a gated 100% coverage requirement and zero concrete callers. Deferred to Phase 2.
A separate fourth Skyline.Interaction.Windowing project in v1. REJECTED — folded into Skyline.Interaction.Ui; the input-without-overlay use case has no v1 caller.
Putting iOS presentation classes (UIKitApprovalUi, UIKit input source) in a shipped Skyline assembly. REJECTED — they go in the app/sample so the one-exclusion (Guard.cs) coverage invariant holds.

Claiming the transfer broker is first-class for GPU surfaces in v1. REJECTED — honestly scoped to text/metadata until the Skyline.Interaction.Gpu bridge exists, because the byte-Stream representation would force a forbidden CPU round-trip.
Trusting the spoofable ActorId message field for locality decisions (FocusActor.IsRemote keying on a string). REJECTED for Phase 2 — locality derives from Sender.Path.

residualRisks: Async/TCS coverage has ZERO precedent in this repo (grep of src/ found no async/await/TaskCompletionSource/IAsyncEnumerable). Even v1's single approval TCS introduces a state machine with cancel/timeout/already-resolved branches. Mitigation is mandatory: inject TimeProvider so deadline/expiry paths use a fake clock; expose Resolve as an internal seam callable directly from a test thread so the lose-the-race and double-resolve branches are hit by direct calls, not races. If any async line lands where only the windowed harness reaches it, the 100% gate is at risk.

The composited overlay still needs SOME windowed coverage (the wgpu encode of the modal panel/indicator) via the single-threaded Skyline.WindowedTests Program.cs harness, which is fragile (Thread.Sleep pacing, hang-guards). Keep the windowed surface to a handful of wire-up Checks; all hit-test/stack/expire/policy logic must be in the GPU-free headless class. If logic leaks into windowed code it becomes hard to gate.

'Skyline handles the approvals UI' is fully true on desktop (composited battery) but on iOS is delivered as a native UIKitApprovalUi in the APP project, not a shipped Skyline assembly. The decision logic is shipped and identical; the pixels are the app's. If the user expects Skyline to ship reusable iOS prompt pixels too, that is a separate reusable-UIKit-component investment that widens the iOS surface and risks a second coverage-exclusion class.

Deferring the full primitive guide means the worked eyes->voice->copy->paste flow is only PARTIALLY first-class in v1 (the authority/approval spine is; the focus/target/transfer machinery is Phase 2). If Starling needs the full flow before Phase 2, the phasing must accelerate — but building it speculatively now is the worse trade.

Zero-copy GPU transfer remains unsolved until the Skyline.Interaction.Gpu bridge (Phase 2+). Surface copy/paste — the payload Starling actually moves — is not first-class until then, and the bridge must be designed to hand over a wgpu handle without contaminating the GPU-free primitives tier.

cover.sh is hardcoded to the three core assemblies. The amendment to add Skyline.Interaction and Skyline.Interaction.Ui to both the coverlet --include flags and the reportgenerator -assemblyfilters, plus registering the new src/test projects in Skyline.slnx, is load-bearing — if missed, the new assemblies are silently unmeasured (a false green) and the gate does not actually apply to them.

When Akka lands in Phase 2, the PinnedDispatcher self-deadlock (any accidental Ask().Result/.Wait()) and the approval-park leak (a lost ApprovalAnswered/timeout) are real hazards. Enforce PipeTo-only, the park-the-asker pattern, scheduler-driven timeouts, and PreRestart-drains-parked-callers — and back them with an analyzer or review rule, since they are easy to reintroduce.
